name: OFAC Screening Agent
description: Screens clients against a previously-ingested, versioned copy of OFAC's actual sanctions list; this agent does not itself call any external API -- the live fetch is performed separately by scripts/ofac-sdn-ingest.js (see docs/SDN-Sanctions-Screening-Design.md). A freshness check runs first: screening against a list older than 7 days blocks (status: not_authoritatively_screened) rather than clears. Exact and near-exact (normalized/transliteration-equivalence) matching tiers only -- fuzzy matching is an explicit, separately-dated fast-follow requiring its own labeled validation set, not built yet. A match at either tier is a hard flag (status: flagged), resolved via the existing dual-control override flow. A genuine no-match against a fresh list produces a real, evidenced 'clear' (list version, tier, and compared fields recorded on the pcm_ofac_results row) -- unlike the prior heuristic version, this 'clear' is authoritative for what it actually checked. Known, stated weak points (transliteration coverage is not exhaustive, no DOB/ID-number filtering yet, name-only screening with no beneficial-ownership detection): see the design doc's matching section.
ais_required_reason: aisVerify() (agents/shared/ais-client.js) targets POST /verify on ais-api, which does not exist -- only POST /ca/verify (certificate verification, a different API shape) is real. The module is also ESM in this CommonJS repo with zero require() callers, so it was never reachable at all. Set false 2026-08-14; see CLAIMS-INVENTORY.txt Addendum 5. Do NOT flip true without building a real, reachable check first -- wiring the module in as-written would 404 and throw (fail-closed) on every agent invocation, taking production down.
sal_logging_reason: salLog() (agents/shared/sal-client.js) is a stub -- its own header says so -- and only writes to stdout; no SAL API exists in this or any other repo to log to. Set false 2026-08-14; see CLAIMS-INVENTORY.txt Addendum 5. Do NOT flip true until a real SAL endpoint exists.
